agordo.why: Main town of the Agordo basin beneath the Agnèr: Duran, Forcella Franche, Forcella Aurine and Cereda start in town, Staulanza, Valles and Giau lie one valley ride away. Quiet, bike shop in neighbouring Taibon.

alassio.why: Seaside resort with bike hotels, spring training base of the teams: Colle San Bernardo, Scravaion, Melogno and the Colle di Nava within a day's range. Railway station on the coastal line.

alleghe-caprile.why: Quiet base beneath the Civetta: Fedaia from Caprile, plus Giau, Staulanza and Duran. Little through traffic, lake and Dolomite walls right on the doorstep.

andermatt.why: Furka, Gotthard, Oberalp, Susten, Nufenen; bike shops, railway station, Alpenbrevet base.

aosta.why: Grand/Petit Saint-Bernard, San Carlo, Cervinia, Pila; bike shops, railway station.

arabba.why: In the middle of the Sellaronda: Pordoi, Campolongo, Falzarego/Valparola and Fedaia start in the village. Bike hotels with bike cellar, rental at the valley station.

bad-kleinkirchheim.why: Nockalmstraße, Turracher Höhe, Villacher Alpenstraße; bike hotels, workshops.

barcelonnette.why: Bonette, Cayolle, Allos, Vars, Champs – seven passes within range. Workshops, cycling accommodation.

bassano-del-grappa.why: The town beneath the Monte Grappa: Semonzo, Romano and Possagno start on the doorstep, the Asiago plateau lies behind. Railway station; rideable almost all year.

bedoin.why: Ventoux village: rental, workshop, cafés, start of the classic climb.

bellagio.why: At the foot of the Ghisallo: the Lombardia loop over Sormano, the Monte San Primo, and by ferry Varenna and the Agueglio. No railway station, but the boats instead.

berchtesgaden.why: Roßfeld panoramic road, Hirschbichl and the loop around the Königssee. Rail link, Alpine backdrop and short approaches from Salzburg.

bormio.why: Stelvio, Gavia, Mortirolo, Foscagno. Many bike shops, rental, bike hotels, thermal baths.

bourg-d-oisans.why: Base for Alpe d'Huez, Galibier, Croix de Fer, Sarenne. Several road bike shops with workshop and rental, Marmotte headquarters.

bourg-saint-maurice.why: Haute-Tarentaise with TGV link: Iseran, Petit-St-Bernard, Cormet de Roselend and Les Arcs. Bike shops with workshop and rental in town.

bovec.why: Soča valley, Vršič, Mangart, Predil; rental, outdoor base.

briancon.why: Izoard, Lautaret/Galibier, Montgenèvre, Granon. Bike shops, railway station, the highest town in France.

brig.why: Valais hub with railway station: Simplon, Nufenen, Furka and Grimsel from the Rhône valley. Low-lying, so rideable early in the year.

bruck-an-der-glocknerstrasse.why: Foot of the Großglockner High Alpine Road; workshop, rental, Zell am See region.

buis-les-baronnies.why: The village in the heart of the Baronnies: Col d'Ey, Fontaube, Soubeyrand, Perty and Macuègne in every direction, almost free of cars, with the Ventoux on the horizon.

canazei.why: Sella, Pordoi, Fedaia, San Pellegrino; bike shops, Sellaronda start.

cavalese.why: Val di Fiemme as a quiet valley base: Manghen, Lavazè, Rolle and San Pellegrino within reach, plus flat valley roads for the day after.

chur.why: Graubünden's rail hub: the Lenzerheide and Arosa start at the station, Flumserberg and Malbun lie a short ride down the Rhine. Low and mild, often warm in autumn too thanks to the foehn.

colmar.why: A town in the Rhine plain with a TGV station; Munster is just under 20 km away, the Schlucht a good 30. Dry and mild, rideable earlier in spring than the valleys.

cortina-d-ampezzo.why: Giau, Falzarego, Tre Cime, Cimabanche; bike shops, wide choice of accommodation.

corvara-alta-badia.why: Sellaronda and Maratona hub: bike hotels, rental, workshops, service points on the passes.

cuneo.why: Fauniera, Lombarde, Agnello, Sampeyre, Maddalena; bike shops, Fausto Coppi Granfondo.

davos.why: Flüela, Albula, Wolfgang; many bike shops, altitude 1,560 m.

domodossola.why: Rail hub on the Simplon line: the Simplon from the south, Macugnaga below the Monte Rosa and the Val Formazza all start from here. Low-lying, rideable early in the year.

feltre.why: Old town on the southern edge of the Belluno Dolomites: Croce d'Aune starts on the doorstep in Pedavena, Grappa, Brocon, Cereda and San Boldo lie within a day's range. Bike hotel with road-bike rental, bike shops, railway station on the Padua–Belluno line; low enough for spring and late autumn.

finale-ligure.why: Italy's mountain-bike capital has the workshops and rental outfits that serve the road bike just as well; the Melogno starts in Finalborgo, Scravaion and Faiallo are day loops. Railway station in town.

gerardmer.why: By the lake on the Lorraine side: the Schlucht, the Col de Grosse Pierre and, via La Bresse, the Bramont. Accommodation of every kind, no railway station.

graz.why: Styria's capital with a rail hub: the Schöckl right from town, the Gaberl and the Weinebene a short approach away in western Styria. Mild climate, long season.

guillestre.why: Gateway to the Queyras: Izoard, Vars, Agnel and Risoul, plus the quiet gorge of the Guil. Campsites and small bike shops instead of ski-resort bustle.

imperia.why: The quieter base between Sanremo and Alassio: Colle San Bartolomeo and Ginestro right behind the town, Nava and Oggia as a loop via Pieve di Teco. Railway station.

innsbruck.why: Kühtai, Brenner, Zirler Berg; wide choice of bike shops, rail hub.

kitzbuehel.why: The Kitzbüheler Horn starts at the edge of town, plus Thurn, Gerlos and Filzensattel. Railway station, rental and a dense choice of hotels.

kranjska-gora.why: Vršič, Predil, Mangart; rental, workshops, bike hotels.

la-bresse.why: A quiet town in the Moselotte valley: the Bramont, Grosse Pierre and the road up to the Hohneck start at the door.

landeck.why: Junction in the upper Inn valley with railway station: Hahntennjoch, Arlberg, Kaunertal glacier road and Silvretta without a long approach.

le-grand-bornand.why: Aravis village: Colombière, Aravis and Croix Fry start in the village. Green side valleys, little traffic, rental in the village.

lecco.why: Rail hub on the eastern arm of Lake Como: Piani dei Resinelli, Culmine di San Pietro, Valcava and Ghisallo within a day's range, bike shops in town.

lienz.why: Sunny town where the Drau, Isel and Puster valleys meet: Gailbergsattel and Kartitscher Sattel on the Dolomitenradrundfahrt loop, plus the Staller Sattel, Kals and, over the Iselsberg, the Grossglockner road. Bike shops with workshop and rental, certified cyclist lodgings, railway station.

livigno.why: Altitude-training resort, bike hotels, workshops; Foscagno, Bernina, Forcola.

locarno.why: On Lake Maggiore with the quiet valley roads of the Verzasca and the Maggia valley on the doorstep, the Alpe di Neggia opposite. Railway station; spring already in March.

lugano.why: Mild Ticino with railway station: Bellavista on the Generoso, Sighignola and Bisbino above the lakes, Monte Ceneri and Alpe di Neggia to the north. Rideable from March.

malaucene.why: The north side of the Ventoux starts in the village, the Madeleine closes the loop to Bédoin; Dentelles, Fontaube and Col d'Ey within a day's range. Bike shops and rental.

malcesine.why: Beneath the Monte Baldo on the eastern shore: Bocca del Creer via Navene, Punta Veleno at Brenzone, plus the road to Riva and Arco. Bike hotels and a long season.

martigny.why: Lower Valais with railway station: Grand-St-Bernard, Forclaz and Champex. At 470 m, one of the earliest bases in the Western Alps.

mayrhofen.why: Zillertal base: Gerlospass and Zillertaler Höhenstraße from the village, valley cycle path for easy days. Zillertalbahn right into the centre, many bike hotels.

meiringen.why: Grimsel, Susten, Grosse Scheidegg; bike shops, railway station.

menton.why: Between Monaco and the border: Col de la Madone and Castillon start at the sea, Sospel and Braus behind, Ventimiglia and the Riviera dei Fiori within an hour. Railway station.

meran-merano.why: Mild valley town for the long season: Jaufen, Timmelsjoch, Gampenjoch and the Vinschgau from the doorstep. Rail link, bike shops, bike hotels.

morbegno.why: Low entry point to the Valtellina: San Marco, Vivione and the approach towards Aprica. Rail right into town, rideable in spring and late autumn.

morzine.why: Chablais classics: Joux-Plane, Ramaz, Avoriaz and Joux Verte from the village. Dense cycling scene with shops, rental and workshops.

munster.why: On the valley floor below the Schlucht: the Col de la Schlucht, Petit Ballon, Platzerwasel and Wettstein start without a ride-in, the Route des Crêtes is one climb away. Railway station on the line to Colmar.

nizza.why: Winter quarters of the peloton: Col d'Èze, Châteauneuf, Vence, Madone and Braus from the city, Turini and Bleine as day loops. Railway station, airport, bike shops.

ponte-di-legno.why: Gavia, Tonale, Mortirolo; bike shops, quieter than Bormio.

prad-am-stilfserjoch.why: Foot of the 48 hairpins, Umbrail, Vinschgau cycle path; rental and workshops.

riva-del-garda.why: The northern tip of Lake Garda: Ballino, Ampola and Ledro, Monte Velo and Santa Barbara on the doorstep, Bocca del Creer and Punta Veleno on the eastern shore. Workshops, bike hotels, season from March.

rovereto.why: Rail hub in the Adige valley with Santa Barbara, Pian delle Fugazze, Bordala and Sommo from the town, Bondone and Lake Garda within a day's range. Mild enough for spring and autumn.

saint-jean-de-maurienne.why: Croix de Fer, Madeleine, Télégraphe/Galibier; railway station, bike shops, Maurienne cycling office.

saint-vincent.why: Spa town in the lower Aosta valley: the Col de Joux on the doorstep, Breuil-Cervinia from Châtillon and the Gressoney valley next door. Châtillon-Saint-Vincent railway station.

san-martino-di-castrozza.why: South ramp of the Rolle beneath the Pale di San Martino: Rolle, Cereda and Croce d'Aune. Quiet, exceptional scenery, hotels from the ski trade.

sanremo.why: Finish of Milan–Sanremo and the winter training ground of the pros: Poggio, Cipressa, Bignone, with Langan, Teglia and Oggia behind. Railway station, bike shops, sea views from every climb.

schladming.why: Enns valley with railway station: Sölkpass, Radstädter Tauern and the Dachstein loop. Bike hotels and rental from the ski trade.

sion.why: The capital of the Valais with a railway station: the Sanetsch, the Grande Dixence and Arolla start right in town, Crans-Montana and Moiry from neighbouring Sierre. Low and dry, so a long season.

soelden.why: Ötztaler headquarters: Timmelsjoch, glacier road, Kühtai; bike shops, rental, bike hotels.

sospel.why: Hinterland of the Côte d'Azur: Turini, Braus, Brouis and Madone. Railway station on the Nice–Tende line and a climate that is rideable almost all year.

spluegen.why: Quiet Rheinwald village between the Splügenpass and San Bernardino, with Julier and Albula following on. Transit runs on the motorway, the pass roads stay empty.

st-moritz.why: Bernina, Julier, Maloja, Albula; bike shops, rental, Engadin cycling routes.

sterzing.why: Jaufen, Penser Joch, Brenner, Pfitscher Joch; bike shops, railway station.

stresa.why: The Mottarone starts outside the hotel; the toll-free climb via Armeno and Gignese, plus Lake Orta and the Alpe di Neggia across the lake. Railway station on the Simplon line.

susa.why: Finestre, Mont Cenis, Sestriere; railway station, bike shops.

tegernsee.why: Lakeside resort in the Bavarian Oberland: the Wallberg on the doorstep, the Spitzingsattel, the Sudelfeld and the Kesselberg nearby. Train from Munich.

thann.why: At the mouth of the Thur valley: the Hundsruck, the Grand Ballon via Willer-sur-Thur and the loop over the Ballon d'Alsace and Bussang. Trains from Mulhouse into town and on up the valley.

toblach-dobbiaco.why: Alta Pusteria with railway station: Tre Cime, Kreuzbergpass and Furkelpass within reach. Bike rental and bike hotels in town, cycle path down the valley.

tolmezzo.why: Carnic hub: Zoncolan, Plöckenpass and Passo di Lanza. Quiet valleys, mild enough for spring and late autumn.

vaduz.why: The capital of Liechtenstein in the Rhine valley: Malbun starts in town, the Furkajoch, the Bödele and Flumserberg are close. Railway stations in Schaan, Buchs and Sargans.

vaison-la-romaine.why: Roman town between Ventoux and Baronnies: Dentelles, Fontaube, Col d'Ey and Soubeyrand as loops, the Ventoux from Malaucène within reach. Quiet and rideable for a long season.

wolkenstein-selva.why: Head of the Val Gardena: Sella and Gardena passes start in the village, Erbe/Würzjoch and the Sellaronda follow on. Many bike hotels, rental and workshops.

oberwiesenthal.why: Germany's highest town at the foot of the Fichtelberg: the Fichtelberg and the Klínovec start at the door, Měděnec and the Auersberg are a day's loop away. Terminus of the Fichtelberg narrow-gauge railway from Cranzahl.

altenberg.why: On the ridge of the eastern Ore Mountains: Cínovec, Komáří vížka, Dlouhá Louka and Bouřňák lie on the Bohemian side, a day's loop away. Station on the Müglitz valley railway from Heidenau near Dresden.

teplice.why: Spa town at the foot of the Bohemian side: Komáří vížka, Cínovec and Dlouhá Louka start in the neighbouring towns of Krupka, Dubí and Osek. Station with connections to Ústí nad Labem and Prague.

freiburg.why: The cycling city at the foot of the southern Black Forest: the Schauinsland starts at the edge of town, the Notschrei, the Kandel and the Wiedener Eck are a day's loop away. Intercity station and plenty of bike shops.

todtnau.why: In the upper Wiese valley between the Feldberg and the Belchen: the Feldbergpass and the Notschrei start in the town, the Wiedener Eck is a short ride away.

baiersbronn.why: In the northern Black Forest on the edge of the national park: the Ruhestein and the Kniebis make a short loop from here, the Black Forest High Road runs along the ridge above.

port-de-pollenca.why: The centre of road-cycling holidays in the north of the island: Femenia, the Coll de sa Batalla and Sa Calobra are day loops, bike hotels and rentals in every street. Rideable from February to November.

soller.why: In the orange valley on the west coast: the Puig Major and the Coll de Sóller start in the town, Sa Calobra lies beyond the Puig Major. Reachable on the historic railway from Palma.
